description: Agent-loop progress primitives + backward-compatible on_progress callback. Adds src/movieintel/agent/progress.py (ProgressPhase, ProgressEvent, PHASE_LABELS) and a keyword-only on_progress callback to run_agent emitting typed ProgressEvents at the verified loop points. Pure Python, no AWS. Foundational: FEAT-002 (worker) and FEAT-004 (OpenAPI reuse of ProgressPhase) depend on this. Independent of all AWS/infra concerns.
steps: Create src/movieintel/agent/progress.py per design Decision 4: `from __future__ import annotations`; `import logging`; `from dataclasses import dataclass`; `from enum import StrEnum`. Define `ProgressPhase(StrEnum)` with members understanding='understanding', searching='searching', comparing='comparing', composing='composing', refused='refused', bounded='bounded'. Define `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class ProgressEvent: phase: ProgressPhase; turn: int; label: str`. Define `PHASE_LABELS: dict[ProgressPhase, str]` with the six labels verbatim from the design (understanding='understanding your question', searching='searching the catalog', comparing='comparing titles', composing='composing the answer', refused='request declined', bounded='stopped at the turn limit'). Add `__all__`.

In src/movieintel/agent/loop.py add `import logging` and a module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` at import. Import ProgressEvent, ProgressPhase, PHASE_LABELS from movieintel.agent.progress. Add the `_emit(on_progress, *, phase, turn)` helper EXACTLY as in the design 'Logger provenance' snippet: no-op when on_progress is None; else `on_progress(ProgressEvent(phase=phase, turn=turn, label=PHASE_LABELS[phase]))` wrapped in `try/except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001` logging at warning with exc_info=True.

Add parameter `on_progress: Callable[[ProgressEvent], None] | None = None` as the last keyword-only parameter of run_agent (after max_turns). Add the five emit sites per design Decision 4 'Emission points', line-anchored to the current control flow: (1) `_emit(on_progress, phase=ProgressPhase.understanding, turn=0)` immediately before `for turn in range(max_turns):`; (2) `_emit(..., phase=ProgressPhase.refused, turn=turn + 1)` immediately before `return safe_refusal()`; (3) `_emit(..., phase=ProgressPhase.bounded, turn=turn + 1)` immediately before the mid-loop `return bounded_response(turns_used=turn + 1)`; (4) inside the `for block in _tool_use_blocks(response):` loop — before `return parsed` (valid final_answer only) emit `composing`/turn+1, emit NOTHING for an invalid final_answer (the FinalAnswerError continue branch), emit `searching`/turn+1 when name in {query_movies, semantic_search}, emit `comparing`/turn+1 when name == compare_movies, emit NOTHING for unknown tools; (5) `_emit(..., phase=ProgressPhase.bounded, turn=max_turns)` immediately before the post-loop `return bounded_response(turns_used=max_turns)`. When on_progress is None, control flow and return value MUST remain byte-for-byte identical.

Add tests/agent/test_loop_progress.py reusing the tests/agent/conftest.py fixtures and builders (config, kb_config, CapturingConverseClient, converse_tool_use/converse_final/converse_guardrail, tool_use_block, make_enriched, StubRepository, FakeAgentRuntime). Pass a list-appending `on_progress` and assert the emitted (phase, turn) sequence for: a single query_movies -> final_answer recommendation (understanding/0, searching/1, composing/2); a semantic_search then compare_movies then final_answer comparison (understanding/0, searching/1, comparing/2, composing/3); a guardrail intervention (understanding/0, refused/1); a non-tool_use stop mid-loop (understanding/0, bounded/1); a never-final tool loop bounded at max_turns=3 (ending bounded/3). Add a case where on_progress raises on every call and assert run_agent still returns the correct result (callback error swallowed).
acceptance_criteria: `uv run pytest tests/agent/test_loop.py` passes with ZERO changes to that file (run_agent without on_progress is byte-for-byte identical) — AC-7.

`uv run pytest tests/agent/test_loop_progress.py` passes and asserts the full emission sequence for recommendation, comparison, guardrail refusal, mid-loop bounded, and post-loop bounded, plus the raising-callback-does-not-break-the-run case — AC-8.
`uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, and `uv run mypy src` pass for the new/changed files.
verification: uv run ruff check src/movieintel/agent/progress.py src/movieintel/agent/loop.py tests/agent/test_loop_progress.py
findings: Public API for downstream FEATs (import from movieintel.agent.progress): ProgressPhase(StrEnum) members understanding/searching/comparing/composing/refused/bounded; ProgressEvent(frozen slots dataclass) fields phase: ProgressPhase, turn: int, label: str; PHASE_LABELS: dict[ProgressPhase, str]. FEAT-004 reuses ProgressPhase for OpenAPI; FEAT-002's worker builds on_progress as `on_progress=Callable[[ProgressEvent], None]`. run_agent signature now ends `..., max_turns: int = MAX_TURNS, on_progress: Callable[[ProgressEvent], None] | None = None`; omitting on_progress is byte-for-byte identical to before. Emission contract the worker's throttled writer must assume: understanding@turn0 before the loop; per turn one event per dispatched tool block in request order (searching for query_movies|semantic_search, comparing for compare_movies, composing before returning a VALID final_answer); refused@turn+1 on guardrail; bounded@turn+1 on a non-tool_use stop and bounded@max_turns post-loop. NO event for an invalid final_answer (loop continues) or an unknown tool. turn is 1-based (turn+1) except the pre-loop understanding (0) and post-loop bounded (max_turns). A mixed-tool turn emits multiple same-turn events (e.g. searching then comparing both at turn+1) -> the design's (phase,turn) throttle collapses them to the LAST block's phase. The callback runs synchronously inside run_agent; a raising callback is swallowed+logged at warning via loop._emit and never fails the run. loop.py gained `import logging` and module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`. NOTE: progress.py has NO `import logging`/logger (FEAT-001 step 1 listed it but it would be an unused-import ruff F401; the logger lives in loop.py per design 'Logger provenance', which is the module that actually logs). Verification env note for later FEATs: tests/conftest.py has a session-scoped autouse `_require_real_dbs` fixture that fails the WHOLE session (erroring every test, including pure-stub ones) when _sqlite/movies.db and _sqlite/ratings.db are absent; those gitignored DBs are missing on this base, which is the known pre-existing not-a-regression failure. To actually run any pytest locally, create placeholder files `_sqlite/movies.db` and `_sqlite/ratings.db` (empty sqlite files suffice for stub-only suites) first, then delete them after; they are gitignored so never committed.
